$comment: PURPOSE AND SHAPE: One note per element in a NIST CPRT export of CSF 2.0 (the JSON record list at $.response.elements.elements[*] — 906 elements in the 2.0.0 export). Flat: functions (6), categories (34), subcategories (185), implementation examples (363) and withdrawal reasons (91) all land at one level, discriminated by the level property — 679 notes. The export's other two element types, the 225 sort keys and 2 parties, are export machinery and are excluded by source.where (see ROW SELECTION below). PROPERTIES: title (the element's short name where it has one), csf_id (the identity), and level (element_type, the discriminator that tells the five concept shapes apart once they share a folder). curie is emitted automatically from source.ontology plus the identifier and is deliberately not declared here. BODY: the element's text field as a single '## Description' section. PROPERTIES-VS-BODY RATIONALE: text was previously a frontmatter 'description' value, and it is the only prose this source carries — 23 to 212 characters for a subcategory, up to 271 for a category, up to 278 for an implementation example. Moving it into the body is the point of this revision: a full sentence in YAML is truncated in Obsidian's property panel, awkward to escape, and invisible to body search, whereas identity and the short level discriminator are exactly what Bases tabulates and what the Tier 2 projection indexes, so they stay in frontmatter. The heading is the literal 'Description' because the schema does not admit templated headings (spec/recipe.schema.json, body_entry.heading) and one recipe emits seven element types; 'Description' is the honest generic for all of them. No H1 is emitted: Obsidian already renders the note title, so a heading repeating the identifier or the title is noise. omit_if_empty (the default) keeps the section off the 12 categories whose text is empty; the 225 text-less 'sort' elements are no longer emitted at all, so omit_if_empty is not what handles them. Note that CPRT leaves title empty on every subcategory and every withdrawal reason (the outcome statement is in text, not title), so those notes carry an empty title property; that is the source's shape, not a projection choice. RIGHTS: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 is a public-domain United States Government work and the CPRT export can be re-downloaded from https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cprt. Recipe, sample output, and screenshots of generated content may all be committed. Corpus provenance and rights posture: https://cybersader.github.io/crosswalker/reference/framework-corpus/. KNOWN GAP 1 — implementation examples cannot be attached to the subcategory they belong to. CPRT ships them as separate elements plus a SIBLING array, $.response.elements.relationships[*] (1,566 edges across four predicates: projection, external_reference, incorporated_into, moved_to). One iterator yields exactly one row array (src/import/parsers/json-source-core.ts), so each example still becomes its own standalone note instead of a section under its subcategory. The grammar's reason has changed: source.joins (SchemaVer 1.9.0) CAN express this shape — the sibling array is reachable as {"iterator": "$.response.elements.relationships[*]", "where": "relationship_identifier = 'projection'"} joined on element_identifier = source_element_identifier, cardinality 'many', selecting dest_element_identifier (field names verified against the shipped export: 1,566 edges, 1,023 of them 'projection'). It is not adopted here because a join changes what a note CONTAINS, and it would bind example identifiers rather than example prose — a separate decision from selecting which rows become notes. The workbook-sourced nist-csf-2-flat recipe can carry the examples only because that source denormalizes them into a cell on the subcategory row. KNOWN GAP 2 — the export's external_reference edges (408 of them) are the same cross-framework mapping content as the workbook's Informative References column. Nothing here emits them, deliberately: they are mapping assertions between two ontologies and belong in a crosswalk / mapping-set import (see recipes/import/crosswalks), not flattened onto the concept note, and the grammar has no per-item split-and-map that could turn them into clean links or CURIEs anyway. ROW SELECTION (SchemaVer 1.9.0 — this replaces what was KNOWN GAP 3, which said no row predicate existed) — the export's element list mixes concepts with export machinery: 225 'sort' ordering keys and 2 'party' elements carry no concept content and must not become notes. source.where is "$not(element_type in ['sort', 'party'])", which admits 679 of the 906 elements. Verified against the shipped 2.0.0 export: 906 = 6 function + 34 category + 185 subcategory + 363 implementation_example + 91 withdraw_reason + 225 sort + 2 party, so the predicate excludes exactly 227 and every remaining element is one of the five concept kinds. This recipe can now be pointed at the whole export; the filtering that used to be a wizard-side or pre-filter concern is stated in the recipe. The predicate runs before identity, CURIE minting, concept_cid and render(), so an excluded element mints no CURIE and cannot surface as an orphan on re-import, and a mistyped field name is refused at preflight rather than silently admitting zero rows.
